# Results — Study 741 (Cicada-Brood)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The (deliberately silly)
claim under test: the springs when a **periodical cicada brood emerges** — the famous
13- and 17-year *Magicicada* mass-emergences — are special for the S&P 500, a
fixed-calendar "cicada indicator" you could front-run because the emergence year has
been known to the year since the previous emergence. A pure spurious-pattern demo,
stated as such. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `a11dcd0a0a72` (SPY total-return close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **SPY total-return** close (`auto_adjust=True` — dividends & splits folded in; labelled total-return, **not** price-only), **8,411 rows, 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30**, fingerprint `a11dcd0a0a72`. SPY is a real, tradable instrument on yfinance, so **no proxy is used** |
| Brood calendar | **hardcoded** table of **30 mapped periodical-cicada brood emergences 1996 → 2025** (every active 17-year brood I–X, XIII, XIV; the three active 13-year broods XIX, XXII, XXIII), de-duplicated to **24 distinct emergence YEARS** — the event unit (one SPY spring per year). Source: UConn / Cooley *Magicicada* brood chart (magicicada.org), cross-checked against the US Forest Service periodical-cicada page and contemporary national coverage |
| Base rate (the punchline) | a brood emerges *somewhere* in **24 of the 30** years 1996-2025 — "a cicada year" is very nearly the whole calendar |
| Event window | first trading session on/after **May 1** of the emergence year (cicadas surface ~mid-May, above ground through late June), held **`WINDOW_K = 42`** sessions (~2 months) for the headline; a **21-session** (~1 month) window cross-checks |
| Baseline / placebo pool | **33** calendar years (1993 → 2025) with a full 42-session May-June window on the SPY tape |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* across independent, non-overlapping emergence years (the correct unit, not a daily panel) on the constant-mean abnormal CAR; Wilson interval on the up-rate; a **20-seed × 1,000-draw random-year placebo** (same May-June window, so the season is controlled); a Welch cicada-vs-non-cicada contrast; the tradability test is the **excess over the every-spring baseline** (alpha), never the raw return vs zero (beta) |
| Execution / costs | one convention: **zero look-ahead by construction** — the emergence year has been on the calendar since the previous emergence 13/17 years earlier, so the overlay may enter at the last April close before the window. One round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV; long-only |

No survivorship (SPY is the whole-market index; the brood table is a fixed astronomical
schedule, not a selected survivor set).

## The headline — mean cicada-spring window return (May 1 → +42 sessions), total-return SPY

| cut | n | raw window | abnormal CAR | one-sample *t* | up-rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| all notable broods | 24 | +2.400% | **+0.385%** | **+0.37** | 18/24 = 75% ([55%, 88%]) |
| 17-year broods only | 23 | +2.626% | +0.607% | +0.57 | 18/23 = 78% ([58%, 90%]) |
| famous marquee only | 5 | +3.755% | +1.706% | +1.19 | 5/5 = 100% ([57%, 100%]) |

The constant-mean **abnormal** CAR (demeaned to strip SPY's ordinary bull drift) is a
statistically-nothing **+0.385%**, one-sample *t* = **+0.37**, across the 24 emergence
years. The up-rate of 75% *looks* suggestive until you notice the every-spring base rate
is already well above 50% (equities drift up), and its Wilson interval [55%, 88%] is
wide. The "famous marquee only" cut (2004, 2007, 2013, 2021, 2024) is 5/5 up with
*t* = +1.19 — a textbook small-sample **selection artifact**: those five nationally-covered
emergences happened to land in up springs, which is exactly the kind of after-the-fact
pattern that builds folklore.

## Random-year placebo — is the cicada-spring mean in the luck cloud?

Draw 24 random years (from the 33-year pool), average their May-June window return,
repeat 20,000 times (20 seeds × 1,000). Every draw uses the same calendar window, so the
placebo controls the seasonal ("sell in May") baseline automatically.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed cicada-spring mean | +2.400% |
| placebo mean (random 24-year springs) | +1.802% (sd 0.606%) |
| every-spring baseline (all 33 years) | +1.801% |
| **right-tail p** (share of null means ≥ observed) | **0.165** |

Cicada springs ran **+60 bps** hotter than an average spring — but a random calendar of
24 springs beats that about **one time in six** (p = 0.165). Inside the luck cloud; not a
signal. The 1-month window says the same: abnormal CAR **+0.142%**, *t* = **+0.20**.

## Cicada vs non-cicada springs (Welch)

| group | n | mean May-June return |
|---|--:|--:|
| cicada springs | 24 | +2.400% |
| non-cicada springs | 9 | +0.201% |
| **Welch *t* (cicada − non-cicada)** | | **+0.874** |

Directionally "cicada springs beat quiet springs", but *t* = +0.87 is nowhere near the
bar — and the non-cicada side has only **9** springs (because a brood emerges in most
years), so this contrast is underpowered by the very base rate that makes the whole
effect a mirage.

## Event anatomy — mean cumulative abnormal return by offset (May-1 anchor)

| offset (sessions) | 0 | 10 | 21 | 31 | 42 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| CAR | +0.304% | +0.517% | +0.142% | +0.444% | +0.385% |
| *t* | +1.52 | +0.92 | +0.20 | +0.45 | +0.37 |

No offset clears |*t*| ≥ 2. The path wanders around zero — the CAR is never more than a
fraction of a percent from flat, and its *t* peaks at a forgettable +1.52 on the very
first in-window session.

## The timer — a pre-schedulable cicada-spring calendar trade

Long SPY over the emergence-spring window only (entry the last April close — zero
look-ahead, the year was always known; exit ~end June), one round trip of one-way costs
charged twice vs NAV, long-only.

| leg | mean | win | *t* **vs 0** (beta) | excess over every-spring baseline | *t* (alpha) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| gross | +240.0 bps | 75% | +2.25 | **+60.0 bps** | **+0.56** |
| net (5 bps) | +230.0 bps | 71% | +2.15 | +50.0 bps | +0.47 |
| net (10 bps) | +220.0 bps | 71% | +2.06 | +40.0 bps | +0.37 |

**The trap, called out:** the *t*-vs-zero (+2.25) looks like an edge but is just SPY's
ordinary two-month bull drift — holding *any* two-month equity window is positive on
average. The honest tradability statistic is the **excess over the every-spring
baseline** (alpha): **+60 bps gross, *t* = +0.56**, fading to +40 bps net of 10 bps costs.
There is no cicada edge — only beta you were always paid for, whether the bugs were out
or not.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic random-walk SPY-like tape (~46 years, matched window vol), a planted extra
return spread across the emergence-spring windows; no network.

| world | one-sample *t* (abnormal CAR) |
|---|--:|
| null (bump = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.15** (sd 0.93), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted bump = +4.0% (seed 741) | **+4.46** |

The null averages *t* ≈ 0 and crosses |*t*| ≥ 2 in **1 of 20** seeds — exactly the ~5%
false-positive rate a correct 5% test *should* show, never a systematic misfire; a
planted +4% spring bump lights up at *t* = +4.46. The detector is unbiased, so the
real-tape *t* = +0.37 is a genuine null, not a sleeping harness. *(A faithful-engine /
power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Cicada-spring abnormal CAR **+0.385%**, one-sample *t* = **+0.37**;
  random-year placebo **p = 0.165**; Welch vs non-cicada springs *t* = **+0.87**; the
  1-month window *t* = +0.20; no event-anatomy offset clears |*t*| ≥ 2. The 75% up-rate
  and the 5/5 "famous broods" cut are small-sample / selection illusions against an
  equity base rate that already drifts up.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The calendar overlay's positive *t*-vs-zero is pure SPY beta;
  the **excess over the every-spring baseline is +60 bps at *t* = +0.56** (gross),
  fading with costs. A perfectly-foreseeable signal that still buys you nothing beyond
  the market's ordinary drift.
- **"Cicada indicator?" — BUSTED.** A brood emerges in 24 of 30 recent years, so "cicada
  years" are almost the whole calendar; the pattern that survives is a coin-flip on top
  of equity drift. This is the demo's whole point — a fixed, famous, foreseeable natural
  calendar produces exactly the noise you'd expect it to.
